The '''Israel Mathematical Union''' ('''IMU''') ({{langx|he|הַאִיגּוּד הַיִשְׂרְאֵלִי לְמָתֶמָטִיקָה}}) is an [[Professional association|association]] of professional [[mathematicians]] in [[Israel]]. It is a member of the [[European Mathematical Society]] and the [[International Council for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], and has reciprocity membership agreements with the [[American Mathematical Society]] and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imu.org.il/affiliated-societies|access-date=24 March 2023|title=Affiliated societies|website=Israel Mathematical Union}}</ref>

The Union was founded on 2 March 1953 and held its first meeting with eleven short lectures on 28 September of that year.<ref name=mactutor>{{cite encyclopedia| last1 = O'Connor | first1 = John J. | last2 = Robertson | first2 = Edmund F. | author-link = John J. O'Connor (mathematician) | author2-link = Edmund F. Robertson |title = The Israel Mathematical Union|url = http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Societies/Israel.html | date = February 2018 | encyclopedia = [[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]] | publisher = [[University of St Andrews]] }}</ref> Early members included [[Binyamin Amirà]], [[Michael Fekete]], and [[Abraham Fraenkel]], who represented the Union at the 1954 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Amsterdam]], as well as [[Shmuel Agmon]], [[Jacob Levitzki]], and Dov Jarden.{{r|mactutor}}

==Prizes==
The Israel Mathematical Union awards four major prizes:
* The [[Erdős Prize|Anna and Lajos Erdős Prize in Mathematics]], awarded to an Israeli mathematician under the age of 41.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imu.org.il/erdos-prize|access-date=24 March 2023|title=The Anna and Lajos Erdős Prize in Mathematics|website=Israel Mathematical Union}}</ref>
* The Levitzki Prize in Algebra, awarded biennially to a young Israeli mathematician for research in [[Abstract algebra|Algebra]] or related areas.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imu.org.il/levitzki-prize|access-date=24 March 2023|title=Levitzki Prize in Algebra|website=Israel Mathematical Union}}</ref>
* The Haim Nessyahu Prize in Mathematics, awarded for outstanding achievements in a mathematical [[Thesis|Ph.D. dissertation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imu.org.il/nessyahu-prize|access-date=24 March 2023|title=Nessyahu Prize|website=Israel Mathematical Union}}</ref>
* The Abarbanel Prize in Applied Mathematics, awarded to an Israeli applied mathematician under the age of 48.<ref>[https://imu.org.il/abarbanel-prize/ "Abarbanel prize"]. ''Israel Mathematical Union''. Retrieved 24 March 2023.</ref>
